subject: bar-headed goose
title: A Goose Flies Where Oxygen Is Half, and Its Heart Doesn't Speed Up

scenes.text: A goose flies where there is half the oxygen. Its heart barely changes.
Bar-headed geese cross the Himalayas. One was tracked flying as high as 7,270 meters.
Up there, the air holds only 30 to 50 percent of the oxygen you breathe at sea level.
Scientists trained geese to fly in a wind tunnel wearing masks that simulated that air.
Flapping burned up to sixteen times more energy than resting. Humans manage about ten times.
Yet their hearts did not beat faster than in normal air, and their blood cooled by up to two degrees.

description:
Bar-headed geese migrate over the Himalayas, where air holds only 30 to 50 percent of sea-level oxygen. One bird was tracked at 7,270 meters.
In a University of British Columbia wind tunnel, their metabolism rose sixteen-fold from rest, compared with about tenfold for humans, while heart rate did not increase.
How high would you get without oxygen?
first_comment: Wind-tunnel tests simulated up to about 9,000 meters. Which migration should we cover next?
